items.followUp: Define a covalent bond and write two properties of covalent compounds.

rubric.why: The definition must identify the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.
rubric.description: Defines an ionic bond as the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the attraction between oppositely charged ions being stated clearly.

rubric.why: Ionic compounds form ordered crystal lattices.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds are crystalline solids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing their crystalline structure.

rubric.why: Strong attractions between ions require considerable energy to overcome.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds have high melting and boiling points.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for high melting point or high boiling point.

rubric.why: Ionic crystals are brittle and may fracture when layers shift.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds are hard and brittle, or that they break easily.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for brittleness.

rubric.why: Ions can move and carry charge when the compound is molten or dissolved in water.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten or in aqueous solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for conductivity in either molten or aqueous state.

modelAnswer: An ionic bond is the electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions.
Ionic compounds are crystalline solids.
They generally have high melting and boiling points.
They are hard and brittle.
They conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water, because their ions are free to move.
They are generally soluble in water and insoluble in non-polar solvents.

items.followUp: Define diffusion and explain two factors that affect diffusion in gases.

rubric.why: Diffusion is the movement or spreading of particles, typically from higher to lower concentration.
rubric.description: Defines diffusion as the spreading or movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to lower concentration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing particle spreading, preferably including movement from higher to lower concentration.

rubric.why: Higher temperature gives particles more kinetic energy and increases their rate of movement.
rubric.description: Explains that increasing temperature increases the rate of diffusion in liquids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct temperature effect.

rubric.why: A larger concentration difference drives faster net diffusion.
rubric.description: Explains that a greater concentration difference or gradient increases the rate of diffusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct concentration effect.

rubric.why: Smaller or lighter particles generally diffuse more rapidly through a liquid.
rubric.description: Explains that smaller or lighter particles diffuse faster than larger or heavier particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct particle-size or mass effect.

modelAnswer: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
Temperature: increasing the temperature makes particles move faster, so diffusion occurs more rapidly.
Concentration difference: a greater difference in concentration between two regions increases the rate of diffusion.
Particle size: smaller, lighter particles generally diffuse faster than larger, heavier particles.

items.followUp: Define solubility and describe how temperature affects the solubility of gases and solids in water.

rubric.why: Solubility specifies the maximum amount of solute that dissolves in a given amount of solvent at a stated temperature to form a saturated solution.
rubric.description: Defines solubility as the maximum amount of solute dissolving in a given amount of solvent at a specified temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the maximum amount and the solvent or saturated-solution condition.

rubric.why: For most solid solutes, solubility in water increases as temperature rises.
rubric.description: States that the solubility of most solids increases with increasing temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the usual trend for solid solutes.

rubric.why: The temperature trend is not universal; a few solids become less soluble as temperature rises.
rubric.description: Notes that the solubility of some solid solutes decreases with increasing temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for recognising the exception among solid solutes.

rubric.why: Gas solubility in liquids generally falls as temperature rises.
rubric.description: States that the solubility of gases in water decreases as temperature increases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the gas-solubility trend.

modelAnswer: Solubility is the maximum amount of a solute that dissolves in a given amount of solvent at a specified temperature to form a saturated solution.
For most solid solutes, solubility in water increases as temperature increases.
For some solid solutes, solubility decreases as temperature increases.
The solubility of gases in water generally decreases as temperature increases.

items.followUp: How many particles are present in one mole of a substance? State the name of this number.

rubric.why: A mole is the SI unit used for amount of substance.
rubric.description: Identifies the mole as the unit or amount of substance.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the mole as an amount or unit of substance.

rubric.why: One mole contains Avogadro's number of particles or entities.
rubric.description: States that one mole contains approximately 6.02 × 10²³ particles (Avogadro's number).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct number of particles or its name.

modelAnswer: A mole is the amount of substance that contains 6.02 × 10²³ particles (entities).
This number is called Avogadro's number.

items.followUp: Write the electronic configuration of calcium (Ca = 20) in shells.

rubric.why: Argon's first two shells contain 2 and 8 electrons.
rubric.description: Gives the first two shell populations as 2 and 8, or the equivalent subshell arrangement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly writing 2, 8 as the first two shell populations.

rubric.why: Argon's third shell contains 8 electrons, completing its configuration.
rubric.description: Completes argon's shell configuration as 2, 8, 8, or gives the equivalent subshell arrangement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the completed correct configuration.

modelAnswer: Argon has 18 electrons.
Its electronic configuration in shells is 2, 8, 8.

items.followUp: State the trend in shielding effect down a group and across a period.

rubric.why: Additional occupied electron shells down a group increase shielding.
rubric.description: States that shielding effect increases down a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct down-group trend.

rubric.why: Across a period, electrons are added to the same main shell while the inner-shell shielding changes little.
rubric.description: States that shielding effect remains approximately constant across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct across-period trend.

modelAnswer: Down a group, the shielding effect increases because the number of occupied electron shells increases.
Across a period, the shielding effect remains nearly constant because electrons are added to the same shell.

items.followUp: Why do elements in the same group have similar chemical properties?

rubric.why: The atomic number is the number of protons and uniquely identifies an element.
rubric.description: States that atomic number gives the number of protons and identifies the element.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking atomic number to proton number or element identity.

rubric.why: Atomic number determines electron arrangement and hence chemical properties; unlike atomic mass, it is unchanged among isotopes of an element.
rubric.description: Explains that atomic number determines electron arrangement and chemical properties, unlike atomic mass which can vary between isotopes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking atomic number to electron arrangement/chemical properties or for noting that isotopes have the same atomic number but different masses.

modelAnswer: Atomic number, unlike atomic mass, is a fundamental property because it gives the number of protons and identifies the element.
It determines the number and arrangement of electrons in a neutral atom, and hence its chemical properties; isotopes can have different masses but the same atomic number.

items.followUp: Name the elements of the second period of the periodic table.

rubric.why: Hydrogen is the first element in the first period.
rubric.description: Names hydrogen as an element of the first period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for hydrogen.

rubric.why: Helium is the second element in the first period.
rubric.description: Names helium as an element of the first period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for helium.

modelAnswer: The elements of the first period are hydrogen (H) and helium (He).
